terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to make the teams and vehicles and see what each one holds.

tasks.title: A team of its own
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `hill_teams.py`, write a class called `Team`. Its `__init__` takes a call sign and a leader, and keeps them in the attributes `call_sign` and `leader` of the new object. Then make `alpha = Team("Alpha", "Kirsty")` and `bravo = Team("Bravo", "Iain")`, and print the leader of each.

Check makes teams of its own, two at a time, and reads the `call_sign` and `leader` of each, to see that every team keeps the values it was made with.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson on a class and on the errors it gives.
Write the class line, then the def line of __init__, with self first.
Keep each value on the new object, through self.
Make alpha and bravo, print their leaders, and run the file.
hints: Look at the `Tent` class in the lesson: it has the same shape, with other names.

Python hands the new object to `__init__` as its first value, so the def line takes `self`, then the call sign, then the leader. A value lands on the object only when it is written to `self` and a dot.
The shape is `class Team:`, then `def __init__(self, call_sign, leader):` moved in under it, with `self.call_sign = call_sign` and `self.leader = leader` moved in under that.

tasks.title: Each vehicle its own kit
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, Dougie's `Vehicle` keeps its `kit` list in the class, so every vehicle shares one list: the rope he put in the van shows up in the pickup too. Change `Vehicle` so that every vehicle has a `kit` list of its own, empty when the vehicle is made. A vehicle still keeps its name in `name`.

Check makes two vehicles of its own, reads the kit of each, puts a stretcher in one, and looks at whether the other's kit stays empty.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on one list for every object.
Run the file and see the rope turn up in the pickup.
Find where the kit list is made, and when that line runs.
Make the list where each new vehicle gets a list of its own, and run the file again.
hints: The line `kit = []` runs once, when Python makes the class, so there is only ever one list.
`__init__` runs once for every new vehicle. A list made there, and kept on `self`, is a new list each time.
The shape is to take out `kit = []` from the class and add `self.kit = []` under `self.name = name` in `__init__`.

tasks.title: Teams from the rota
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, write a function called `make_teams` that takes a list of `(call sign, leader)` tuples and gives back a list of `Team` objects, one for each tuple, in the same order. Leave the list it is given as it was. Print the leader of each team it gives back for `rota`.

Check calls `make_teams` with lists of its own, an empty one among them, and looks at whether it gives back a list of teams, each a new `Team` with the call sign and leader of its tuple. It uses its own `Team`, so a mistake in Task 1 does not count here.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on many objects from data.
Start an empty list, and go through the tuples with a for loop, taking each apart into its two values.
Make a new Team in each round of the loop, and add it to the list.
Give the list back, and print each leader for rota.
hints: Each call of `Team(...)` makes a new object. One team made before the loop and changed in each round is still one object, put in the list several times.
A tuple of two values comes apart into two names on the for line, and `Team` takes those two values, not the tuple.
The shape is `teams = []`, then `for call_sign, leader in rows:` with `teams.append(Team(call_sign, leader))` under it, then `return teams`.
